report.summary: Chunk 8 of index.py: finalizes index build with memoized clone passes, builds resolver with doc units, computes churn/scoring, and conditionally adds python_naming and document/wiki extras.
risks: _RESOLVER_CACHE | medium | The resolver cache key includes docs_on, types_on, wiki_on, but the comment warns about unscoped builds overwriting scoped resolvers; key may still be insufficient if other scope fields change. | Verify that all relevant scope attributes are included in _scope_key.

extra["python_naming"] | low | The naming report is only added when scope.center or naming_report["ambiguous_count"] is truthy, but the comment says 'a no-center repo with no collisions gets the dict it always got' – this is uncheckable without prior code. | Confirm that prior code always produced a dict without python_naming key.

doc_links and wiki_on | medium | wiki_on adds 'wiki' extra with note about type_refs being unresolved; but doc_links variable is used in doc_rev construction but not in wiki block – potential inconsistency. | Check if doc_links is intended to be used in wiki section or if it's a separate variable.

extra["documents"] | low | The document extra includes 'excluded_from' list; the comment says a consumer must be able to read WHY. But the exclusion reasons are hardcoded strings, not derived from actual exclusion logic. | Ensure the exclusion list matches the actual scan exclusions.

memo reuse | low | Comment claims memo is shared across three passes to avoid recomputing normalization/abstraction; but this is an optimization claim that cannot be verified without seeing CloneMemo implementation. | Verify CloneMemo actually caches and reuses results.

handoff.purpose: Finalize index build: run clone passes with shared memo, build resolver (including doc units), compute churn and scoring, and conditionally add python_naming and document/wiki extras.

claims.text: Normalization and abstraction are the two most expensive operations in the scan.
claims.why: The chunk does not contain any profiling or cost data to verify this claim.

claims.text: Scoped to this call and dropped with it -- a module-level cache would leak across scans.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the lifecycle of 'memo' or whether it is dropped; 'memo' is a local variable, but whether it is dropped after the function returns is not verifiable here.

claims.text: CodeUnits are not JSON-serializable so it lives in a side cache, never in the returned (serializable) index dict.
claims.why: The chunk does not serialize the index dict or show that CodeUnits are not JSON-serializable.

claims.text: Keying it by root alone made the two caches disagree: an unscoped build of the same root overwrote the scoped resolver, and a later scoped slice hit _INDEX_CACHE (so no rebuild repaired it) and resolved callees against a defs_by_file that still contained SHELL units -- pulling a vendored body into a slice the center was supposed to exclude.
claims.why: The chunk does not show _INDEX_CACHE or the previous keying scheme; this is a historical bug fix description.

claims.text: DOCUMENT SECTIONS ARE IN THE RESOLVER, AND ONLY THERE. ``build_resolver`` uses units for one thing -- ``defs_by_file`` -- and ``resolve`` consults that map only for the querying file itself and for files it IMPORTS. Nothing imports a document (document links are kept out of ``import_targets_by_rel`` on purpose), so a heading can never be returned as the resolution of a code identifier.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the implementation of build_resolver or resolve, nor the contents of import_targets_by_rel.

claims.text: What it CAN do is the thing the defect needs: ``context_plan._symbol_names`` reads ``defs_by_file`` wholesale to build the BM25 lexical corpus, so heading titles become searchable evidence and a specification stops being invisible to the planner.
claims.why: The chunk does not reference context_plan or BM25 corpus; this is a cross-file claim.

claims.text: Documents stay OUT of ``all_units`` so no clone pass sees prose.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the contents of all_units or how doc_units are separated.

claims.text: AND NOTHING TYPE-SHAPED IS IN THAT ARGUMENT LIST (invariant I2). The type layer resolves annotations against its OWN ``typegraph.types_by_file`` table, which is never merged in here. If a class were in ``defs_by_file`` it would displace a same-named function (``resolve`` takes the first match), and if a field name were, ``graph.callees`` -- which resolves EVERY identifier token in a body -- would turn ``path``, ``root``, ``name``, ``line``, ``source`` into fabricated CALL edges in every slice.
claims.why: The chunk does not show typegraph, graph.callees, or the defs_by_file construction; this is a design invariant claim.

claims.text: HOTSPOTS ARE A CODE-HEALTH RANKING, so documents are not in it. Left in, a 1,800-line handoff scores loc/50 = 36 -- competitive with real rot, with no code in it at all -- and ``spine/picker.hotspot_candidates`` turns a hotspot row into a work item reading 'extract the long functions, keep every public name and signature'. Against a document that instruction is self-contradictory and nothing downstream rejects it.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the implementation of score_modules or hotspot_candidates; this is a design rationale.

claims.text: An unconfigured repo with nothing to report must produce a byte-identical index to before this change, so the key is present only when there is something to say.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the previous index format or confirm byte-identity; the code conditionally adds the key, but the claim about byte-identity cannot be verified.

claims.text: A no-center repo with no collisions -- the case every unconfigured repo is in -- gets the dict it always got.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the previous dict structure; the code conditionally adds 'python_naming' only when center or ambiguous_count is truthy, but the claim about 'dict it always got' is unverifiable.

claims.text: With documents off the returned dict has no document keys at all, so a pre-document consumer sees the dict it always saw and ``forest``/``slice``/``graph`` take their unchanged paths by construction rather than by a flag test.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the returned dict or the forest/slice/graph consumers; the code only conditionally populates extra['documents'] when docs_on is True, but the claim about unchanged paths is unverifiable.

claims.text: With documents ON, the block is never silent about what it withheld -- an unresolved link is a relation the map is NOT showing, and an unreported one is indistinguishable from a document that links to nothing.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the reporting of unresolved links; the code includes n_links_unresolved but does not show that every unresolved link is reported.

claims.text: A link is not an import: it carries no name binding, it does not make the target a dependency, and folding it in would silently move ``fan_in``, ``fenced_dominance`` and every reachability answer derived from the import graph. The forest is a MULTIPLEX graph precisely so a second kind of relation gets its own layer instead of contaminating one.
claims.why: The chunk does not show the forest graph or how fan_in/fenced_dominance are computed; this is a design rationale.

claims.text: OWN LAYER, never merged into document_links. A doc->doc wikilink and a doc->code reference are different relations, and `type_refs` are names NOBODY resolved -- publishing them as edges would assert a binding that was never made.
claims.why: The chunk does not show document_links or how wiki links are stored; the code adds a separate 'wiki' key in extra, but the claim about not merging is unverifiable.

observations.what: The memo object is created locally and passed to three cluster functions, but the comment says it is scoped to this call and dropped with it. This is consistent with local variable lifetime.

The _RESOLVER_CACHE assignment uses all_units + doc_units, but the comment says 'documents stay OUT of all_units' – they are concatenated here, so they are included in the resolver but not in the clone passes.

The extra dict is conditionally populated with 'python_naming' and 'documents'/'wiki' keys. The comment claims byte-identical index when these are absent, but this cannot be verified without seeing the return statement.
The doc_rev defaultdict is constructed but not used anywhere in this chunk; it may be used later or is dead code.
